subject: PayFlow: surge of timeouts and 5xx/429s — immediate mitigation + exec check-in
messages:
From: Jude Lawson <jude@payflow.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-14T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429s + timeouts affecting payments checkout

Dylan —

We started seeing a large increase in 5xx and 429 errors hitting our checkout endpoints around 16:25 PST today. Our users are getting timeouts, and retrying is making things worse (we're seeing a retry amplification pattern). This is impacting live transactions (about ~3% of checkout attempts failing). Can you triage? Our team captured logs and a HAR file — attached is a zip with samples.

We need an ETA for a mitigation and want to schedule an executive update in case this becomes a longer outage.

Thanks,
Jude Lawson
Head of Ops, PayFlow

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-14T18:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Spike in 5xx/429s + timeouts affecting payments checkout

I've spun up a war room and started digging. Early observations:
- We see a burst of 429s from the edge proxy (rate limiter) followed closely by upstream 5xx from the model-serving pool.
- Error traces point to sustained queue growth on a subset of pods; KV cache hit-rate dropped for a specific model variant.
- No infra deploys at 16:00 in prod, but autoscaler did scale up some pools; suspect autoscaling lag + aggressive client retry behavior.

Opened SUP-1247 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1247) and attached a dashboard snapshot.

Immediate mitigations I'm proposing:
1) Temporarily raise edge rate limit for PayFlow routes to blunt 429s (30m window) — low-risk, can be reverted.
2) Apply a conservative circuit-breaker on upstream path to stop retry amplification.
3) Increase pre-warmed instances for the affected model variant to reduce cold-start queueing.

I'll run the rate-limit patch first (5–10m). Dev, please prep a small routing config change for canary deploy once we confirm.

—Laura
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLO-dashboard-snapshot.png

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-14T18:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Spike in 5xx/429s + timeouts affecting payments checkout

Thanks — I dug into the traces referenced in the logs. Findings:
- A small percentage of requests (1.8%) are hitting a model variant that has a larger sequence length distribution; KV cache misses cause higher latency and some backpressure to the serving queue.
- Our gateway's retry logic is configured to aggressively retry on 5xx/timeout for that customer route. With the burst, retries are amplifying the load.

Proposed immediate changes (I can push in next 20–30m):
A) Reduce retry attempts for PayFlow route from 3 -> 1 and increase retry backoff to 5s.
B) Add a short-lived (30m) soft quota on concurrent requests from their account to flatten spikes.
C) Canary a routing config that pins PayFlow to the lower-latency model variant while we scale pre-warmed workers.

If approved I'll coordinate the canary and monitor. Expected timeline: rate-limit change (5–10m), retry config change + canary (20–30m), scaling nodes (10–15m).

—Dev
Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1247

Jude —

Thanks for the report and for the logs. We are taking the following immediate steps:
- Applying a temporary edge rate-limit increase for your routes to reduce 429 propagation.
- Applying a circuit-breaker and reducing retry aggressiveness on your account.
- Pinning a canary to the lower-latency model variant and scaling pre-warmed workers.

We'd like to schedule an executive 15-min check-in at 1:00pm PT tomorrow (Jan 15) to review impact and next steps — will that work for your team? If so we will invite leadership from both sides.

For transparency: we may propose a short credit for affected transactions depending on final impact analysis. We'll confirm during the check-in.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-15T13:40:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident exec summary & action tracker — PayFlow outage window (Jan 14)

Folks — quick exec summary for leadership and follow-up items after the PayFlow incident. Sending from my mailbox for visibility; I'll push to the company incident tracker after we agree on items.

Timeline (high level):
- 16:25 PST (Jan 14): PayFlow reports surge of 429/5xx and timeouts.
- 16:30–17:00 PST: SRE war room engaged; rate-limit and circuit-breaker mitigations applied.
- 17:15 PST: Retry policy reduced and routing canary pinned; pre-warmed workers scaled.
- 17:45 PST: error rate reduced to baseline (<0.1%), customer reported checkout flow stabilized.

Root causes (summary):
1) Retry amplification from customer client + aggressive gateway retry policy.
2) Transient KV cache miss on a specific model variant that increased latency for a subset of requests.
3) Autoscaler reaction lag combined with cold starts increased queuing.

Immediate follow-ups (owners & ETA):
- Laura: Add a targeted alert for rising queue depth on model-serving pool (ETA: 48h).
- Dev: Implement per-account retry ceiling (policy change) and add a canary test for model-variant routing (ETA: 24h for rollout to canary, 72h full rollout).
- Logan: Review autoscaler thresholds and pre-warm policies with infra (ETA: 5 business days).
- Monica/Dylan: Coordinate customer exec debrief and finalize compensation (if any) — update before Jan 18.
- Ops: Document runbook gap where edge rate-limits and application retries interact; add example playbook to runbooks repo (ETA: 72h).

Risks & asks for leadership:
- We should consider relaxing SLOs for very short cold-start spikes or explicitly document warmup SLO exceptions. Approve a small credit pool (suggested: up to $15k) to be used at CS discretion for verified loss.
- Need sign-off to push retry-policy changes as config rollback is easy but must be coordinated with client SDK docs.

Attachments: SLO-dashboard-snapshot.png, SUP-1247 link, proposed-mitigation-plan.docx

I'll convert these into a formal postmortem with timelines and metrics once we close SUP-1247. Please reply with any changes or approvals.

—Dylan
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
